data.content_ref: inline:The aggregation argument assumes panel errors are 'largely uncorrelated' because members follow the same checklist, but the shared checklist is itself a common input that induces correlated, not independent, errors. The target offers no causal mechanism establishing why non-experts applying an identical explicit checklist would produce uncorrelated errors; the more natural causal story is shared systematic bias from the common checklist and training. Its own countercondition concedes a systemic checklist error induces shared bias, but the core mechanism never rules out the milder, omnipresent version: the checklist's design causes correlated mistakes even absent a 'systemic error.' Thus aggregation may amplify rather than cancel the dominant error component.
